summary: A class defines a new type with its own fields. Each object you create from the class gets its own copy of those fields.
notes: __init__(self) runs every time you call Student().
self.name = "" creates the name field on the new object.
maya.name = "Maya" changes only maya. jordan keeps its own empty name.
pitfall: Writing maya = Student without parentheses stores the class itself, not a new object. Setting maya.name then changes the class, not a student.
